clinician.trajectory_summary: A 30-year-old male initially presented with hemoptysis, chest distress, shortness of breath, and palpitation, which was initially suspected as pneumonia and treated symptomatically. A year later, during a subsequent admission, pulmonary CT showed findings compatible with diffuse alveolar hemorrhage (DAH). Concurrent lab findings included leukocytosis, elevated hemoglobin/hematocrit, elevated liver enzymes, hyperglycemia, elevated creatinine, proteinuria, and glucosuria. Bronchoalveolar lavage (BAL) showed macrophage predominance and ruled out common autoimmune and infectious causes for DAH. An abdominal CT scan subsequently revealed a large left adrenal mass.

key_supporting_evidence.claim: Initial presentation included hemoptysis, paroxysmal chest distress, shortness of breath, and palpitation.
Pulmonary CT on a subsequent admission showed patchy high-density shadow and ground-glass opacity, compatible with diffuse alveolar hemorrhage (DAH).

On admission, lab results showed leukocytosis (WBC 23,720/mm3), elevated hemoglobin (18.1 g/dl) and hematocrit (52%), elevated ALT (62 IU/L), AST (58 IU/L), LDH (326 IU/L), hyperglycemia (blood glucose 297 mg/dl), elevated serum creatinine (114 ummol/L), proteinuria, and glucosuria.
Bronchoalveolar lavage (BAL) reported macrophage (86%), lymphocyte (1.5%), and neutrophil (12.5%).
An abdominal CT scan discovered a left adrenal mass measuring 69 x 61 x 62 mm.

ruled_out_or_less_likely_alternatives.basis: Initial diagnosis was suspected pneumonia, but patient was discharged without further evaluation after symptom relief. Subsequent workup revealed DAH and an adrenal mass, pointing to a different underlying etiology.
Further laboratory tests showed anti-DNA, c-ANCA, anti-MPO, ANA, and anti-GBM antibodies were negative (E003).
Blood and sputum cultures were negative (E003).

remaining_uncertainties: Biochemical confirmation of pheochromocytoma (e.g., plasma or 24-hour urine metanephrines and catecholamines levels).
More definitive confirmation of diffuse alveolar hemorrhage (e.g., presence of hemosiderin-laden macrophages in BAL or serial BAL red cell counts).
